title: HVAC Airflow Particle Visualization with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that visualizes HVAC airflow through a simplified architectural cross-section with a physics debug overlay.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 18) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 7) with intensity 0.8.
- Background color: #1a1a2e (dark blue-gray).
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## Architecture Layout
- Create a simplified room cross-section using BoxGeometry walls:
  - Floor: 20x0.3x10 at y=-2, gray material.
  - Ceiling: 20x0.3x10 at y=6, gray material.
  - Left wall: 0.3x8x10 at x=-10, light gray material.
  - Right wall: 0.3x8x10 at x=10, light gray material.
  - Internal partition wall: 0.3x5x10 at x=0, y=0.5 (does not reach ceiling, leaving a 3-unit gap at top for airflow).
- Add two HVAC duct boxes (blue-tinted semi-transparent material, opacity 0.3):
  - Supply duct: 3x1x2 at position (-7, 5.2, 0) on ceiling of left room.
  - Return duct: 3x1x2 at position (7, 5.2, 0) on ceiling of right room.
- Mark supply duct outlet (bottom face) and return duct inlet (bottom face) with green and red wireframe planes respectively.

## Particle System
- Implement a custom particle system with 500 particles max using THREE.Points with BufferGeometry.
- Each particle has: position (vec3), velocity (vec3), lifetime (float), temperature (float 18-30°C).
- Particles emit from the supply duct outlet at a configurable rate (default 10 particles/frame).
- Initial particle velocity: downward (-y) with slight random spread, magnitude ~0.03-0.06 units/frame.
- Particle physics each frame:
  - Apply gravity: vy -= 0.0002 per frame.
  - Apply buoyancy based on temperature: vy += (temperature - 22) * 0.0001 (warm air rises).
  - Apply drag: velocity *= 0.998.
  - Wall collision: reflect velocity component and clamp position when hitting walls/floor/ceiling. Use coefficient of restitution 0.3.
  - Partition wall collision: particles must navigate over the partition gap.
  - Near return duct: apply suction force pulling particles toward return duct center, force magnitude 0.001 / distance.
- Particle color: map temperature to color gradient (blue=18°C to red=30°C) using HSL interpolation.
- Particle size: 0.15, with alpha fading as lifetime decreases.
- Particles reaching the return duct inlet (within 1.5 units) are recycled.
- Particles exceeding lifetime of 600 frames are recycled.

## Physics Debug Overlay
- Toggled by pressing 'D' key.
- When active, render:
  - Velocity vectors as small lines from each particle (scaled by 20x for visibility) using a separate LineSegments object with green color.
  - Collision bounding boxes for all walls as wireframe boxes (yellow).
  - Force field visualization around return duct: three concentric wireframe circles (radii 2, 4, 6) in red with decreasing opacity.
  - A text overlay (HTML div) showing: total active particles, average particle speed, average temperature, particles recycled count.

## UI Controls (HTML overlay)
- A panel in top-left corner with dark semi-transparent background:
  - 'Emission Rate' slider: range 1-30, default 10. Controls particles emitted per frame.
  - 'Supply Temperature' slider: range 18-30, default 22, step 0.5. Sets initial temperature of new particles.
  - 'Fan Power' slider: range 0.5-3.0, default 1.0, step 0.1. Multiplier on initial velocity magnitude and suction force.
  - 'Pause/Resume' button: toggles simulation.
  - 'Reset' button: clears all particles and resets counters.
  - 'Toggle Debug' button: same as pressing D.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- particleCount: number of currently active particles (integer).
- avgSpeed: average speed (magnitude of velocity) of all active particles (float).
- avgTemperature: average temperature of all active particles (float).
- recycledCount: total particles recycled since last reset (integer).
- emissionRate: current emission rate from slider (integer).
- supplyTemperature: current supply temperature from slider (float).
- fanPower: current fan power multiplier from slider (float).
- isPaused: boolean, whether simulation is paused.
- debugOverlayVisible: boolean, whether debug overlay is shown.
- elapsedFrames: integer frame counter since last reset.
- particlePositions: array of {x, y, z} for first 10 active particles (for probing).
- particleVelocities: array of {vx, vy, vz} for first 10 active particles.
- particleTemperatures: array of floats for first 10 active particles.
- collisionCount: total wall collisions detected since last reset (integer).
- suctionActiveCount: number of particles currently within suction range (distance < 6 from return duct center) (integer).

Ensure __3D_STATE__ is initialized before the first frame with sensible defaults (particleCount=0, isPaused=false, debugOverlayVisible=false, etc.).
physics_constraints: Particles must obey: gravity (constant downward acceleration 0.0002/frame), buoyancy proportional to (temp - 22°C), drag coefficient 0.998 per frame, wall reflections with restitution 0.3, suction force inversely proportional to distance from return duct. All positions must remain within room bounds: x in [-10,10], y in [-2,6]. No NaN values in any particle property. Average speed must remain bounded and non-zero when particles are active. Temperature must stay in [18,30] range.
